title: Retention fence enforcer and eviction-proof manifest for prompts/requests/metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a storage-layer "retention fence" enforcer that guarantees per-route/tenant TTLs for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics, and emits a tamper-evident eviction proof manifest for compliance evidence. This ticket covers the enforcer daemon, the tombstone/manifest schema, integration hooks for the request ingestion pipeline, and a minimal console hook to fetch proof bundles for legal/audit requests.
acceptance_criteria: Retention fence daemon enforces TTLs at the storage shard level and prevents reads of items past their configured TTLs
Eviction-proof manifest (signed, timestamped) is generated for every purge window containing SHA256 hashes of deleted object batches and retention policy metadata
Manifest upload to evidence bucket completes within purge window and is queryable via internal compliance API
Per-route overrides respected: route-level TTL > tenant default > global default, with explicit 'immutable' flag blocking deletion when set
Unit and integration tests covering eviction timing, backfill of missed tombstones, and manifest verification logic
Performance impact < 5% p95 write latency on peak ingestion during a purge window on Canary cluster
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight retention fence daemon that subscribes to retention schedule events from config service and coordinates shard-level purges
Use a two-phase tombstone approach: mark-for-delete epoch, then physical deletion after confirmation to support short legal-hold rollbacks
Manifests are JSONL with fields: manifest_id, tenant_id, route, policy_version, purge_window_start, purge_window_end, deleted_keys_hashes[], signature
Signature scheme: HMAC-SHA256 using KMS-managed key; include a canonicalization step to ensure consistent hashes for cross-region verification
Avoid scanning entire datasets at purge time: leverage retention shadow index that stores (expiry_ts, object_key) and supports range deletes
Backpressure behavior: when eviction backlog grows > 3x window, automatically throttle low-priority routes and emit alert to SRE channel
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): deploy retention fence to canary cluster (internal-only tenants) with dry-run mode where manifests are generated but deletions are not executed
Phase 2 (Pilot): enable physical deletion for two low-volume tenants and validate proof manifest consumption via compliance API
Phase 3 (Gradual): enable on 10% of production tenant traffic using traffic-annotation header to verify no false positives
Phase 4 (Full): global rollout with automated scaling policies; enable hard delete and evidence export to customer-configured S3/KMS endpoints
qa_plan: Automated test suite: retention index unit tests, tombstone lifecycle tests, manifest verification tests
Manual tests: create time-skewed objects, set route TTLs, run purge window and verify objects become inaccessible and manifests contain expected hashes
Chaos test: simulate partial manifest upload failure and verify retry/exponential backoff and idempotent manifest ingestion
Compliance verification: run end-to-end with legal-hold toggle and ensure manifests reflect held objects and do not include them
